title: Being Difficult Together
description:
Another hard day.

Dae-un came in and didn't ask. Just sat.

'How are you doing today?'

The night {name} had said it out loud for the first time. 'Honestly — things have been hard lately.'
Her: 'I know. I just want to be difficult with you.'

choices.text: "Still hard. But better with you here."
choices.result_text:
She laughed a little, then said nothing.
Just stayed.

That offer to share the difficulty — it was still valid.
That said a lot.

She looked skeptical. Didn't push.

Better or just numb — she probably couldn't tell.
Neither could {name}, honestly.

title: The Feed
description:
Days later.

The photo surfaces sometimes.
White dress. A wide smile.

{name} doesn't resent her.
It's just that the smile feels unfamiliar.

Could a smile like that ever come.

choices.result_text:
Took a while to land. But today it was real.

Different destinations. She reached hers.
{name} is still moving toward theirs.

Did it. No like, no comment.

She's living her life. {name} is living theirs.
Just a pause. Then keep going.

title: The Café Promise
description:
Dae-un finished her first day at the Gangnam office.

'How was it?'
'Everyone walks so fast there.'

She laughed.

The promise from before: 'When you get to Gangnam, we'll hit that café nearby.'

choices.result_text:
Gangnam café. Dae-un looked out the window.
'I can't believe I work here now.'

{name} was still on the outside of this neighborhood.
But at least — sitting here today with coffee. First time.

choices.text: "I'll be there soon. Then we'll go."
choices.result_text:
'I know,' she said.

The promise still stands.
The day {name} walks through that neighborhood as a resident rather than a visitor — then the café.

title: Good, Said Dad
description:
Sunday evening call.

Dad brought it up.
'That man was in the news. The one you called me about.'

{name} paused.

choices.text: "Yes. But I learned things from him."
choices.result_text:
Dad thought about it, then:
'Even a flawed person teaches something.'

An unexpected kind of comfort.
What Sang-chul gave {name} — that was separate from who Sang-chul was.

'Right,' Dad said. Moved on.

His name in a newspaper. Then just a name.
{name} felt the weight shift. Slightly lighter.

title: Two Things at Once
description:
Without him, {name} might not be here.
Because of him, Dad suffered for years.

Both are true at the same time.

Today that came back without warning.

choices.text: Accept both — that's the most honest framing
choices.result_text:
People you can't thank and can't blame — there are a few of those in every life.

Holding both without resolving them. That's actually closer to real.
A little less stuck.

choices.text: Still not resolved — more time needed
choices.result_text:
Not resolved. His name still catches at something.

Being unresolved isn't weak. It's not pretending.
When resolution comes, it'll come.

title: Finding It
description:
Message from Ji-yeon.

'Remember how we both said we were still figuring out our own way? I think I found mine.'

{name} recalled the alley. That conversation about paths.

choices.result_text:
Ji-yeon sent a small emoji.

Not deep friends — but people who knew the same question at the same time.
That's a certain kind of connection. Enough for Seoul.

'That's still figuring it out,' Ji-yeon replied.

True. Wandering with intention is also a path.
{name} smiled a little and put the phone down.
